summaryBox.title: Proof Methodology
summaryBox.takeaway: To establish X = Y in rigorous mathematics, always prove both X ⊆ Y and Y ⊆ X via element-chasing.

conceptBreakdown.content:
| Law Name | Union Version ($\cup$) | Intersection Version ($\cap$) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Idempotent Laws** | $A \cup A = A$ | $A \cap A = A$ |
| **Identity Laws** | $A \cup \emptyset = A$ | $A \cap U = A$ |
| **Domination / Annihilation** | $A \cup U = U$ | $A \cap \emptyset = \emptyset$ |
| **Commutative Laws** | $A \cup B = B \cup A$ | $A \cap B = B \cap A$ |
| **Associative Laws** | $(A \cup B) \cup C = A \cup (B \cup C)$ | $(A \cap B) \cap C = A \cap (B \cap C)$ |
| **Distributive Laws** | $A \cup (B \cap C) = (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)$ | $A \cap (B \cup C) = (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)$ |
| **De Morgan's Laws** | $(A \cup B)' = A' \cap B'$ | $(A \cap B)' = A' \cup B'$ |
| **Absorption Laws** | $A \cup (A \cap B) = A$ | $A \cap (A \cup B) = A$ |
| **Complement Laws** | $A \cup A' = U$ | $A \cap A' = \emptyset$ |
| **Involution / Double Complement** | $(A')' = A$ | — |
| **Relative Complement Identities** | $A \setminus B = A \cap B'$ | $A \setminus (B \cup C) = (A \setminus B) \cap (A \setminus C)$ |

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Rigorous Proof of De Morgan’s Law
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Rigorous Proof of De Morgan’s Law
conceptBreakdown.content:
To prove set equality $(A \cup B)' = A' \cap B'$, we must establish mutual inclusion:

1. **PART 1: Show $(A \cup B)' \subseteq A' \cap B'$**
   - Let $x \in (A \cup B)'$ be arbitrary $\implies x \notin (A \cup B) \implies \neg(x \in A \lor x \in B) \implies (x \notin A) \land (x \notin B) \implies x \in A' \cap B'$. Thus $(A \cup B)' \subseteq A' \cap B'$.

2. **PART 2: Show $A' \cap B' \subseteq (A \cup B)'$**
   - Let $y \in A' \cap B'$ be arbitrary $\implies (y \in A') \land (y \in B') \implies (y \notin A) \land (y \notin B) \implies \neg(y \in A \lor y \in B) \implies y \notin (A \cup B) \implies y \in (A \cup B)'$. Thus $A' \cap B' \subseteq (A \cup B)'$.

**Conclusion**: $(A \cup B)' = A' \cap B'$. $\blacksquare$
